comment: Deployment descriptor. Every component maps 1:1 to a module that already runs locally; nothing here is a re-implementation. See docs/deployment/catalyst-runtime.md for why cip-api is an AppSail service, not an Advanced I/O function.

functions.name: cip_refresh
functions.description: Runs one pipeline stage (ingest, data_quality, intelligence, retention) per Circuit invocation.

appsail.name: cip-console
appsail.description: Static React console. Serves frontend/dist and proxies /api to the cip-api AppSail service.

appsail.name: cip-api
appsail.description: Runs the FastAPI application (ksp_cip.interface.api.main:get_app) under uvicorn. Replaces a prior Advanced I/O function whose handler had no documented ASGI bridge -- see docs/deployment/catalyst-runtime.md.

datastore.note: Table definitions are generated from the same schema file the SQLite adapter applies, so the two backends cannot drift. Provisioning is manual/reviewed, not an application-startup executescript() call -- see docs/deployment/catalyst-schema.md.

buckets.name: cip-ingest
buckets.description: NDJSON landing zone and generated exports.

cron.name: cip_nightly_trigger
cron.description: Invokes the cip_nightly Circuit once a day. A Circuit has no schedule of its own; Cron is the component that triggers it.
cron.comment: VERIFIED from the Catalyst Cron docs: a cron's schedule point may be a function, a third-party URL, or a Circuit; schedule types are One Time and Recursive; the minimum recursive frequency is one hour (daily is well inside that). NOT VERIFIED: the exact console/CLI field names below -- Cron is created through the console or CLI and Zoho does not publish a committed-file schema for it, so treat this block as the reviewed provisioning intent (what to create, with which schedule and target), not as a file the CLI ingests. Record the real field names here once the cron is created against a live project.
